question.text: How many additional US states will enact bans on cultivated meat before July 2027?
question.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves as the number of additional US states which enact a law prohibiting the sale of cultivated meat before July 1, 2027.

The following states will not be considered for this question:

* Alabama
* Florida 
* Indiana
* Mississippi
* Montana
* Nebraska
* South Dakota
* Texas 

If no new prohibitions on the sale of cultivated meat become law in any additional US state before July 1, 2027, this question resolves as **Zero**.

research:
I found no additional state that has enacted a qualifying ban as of 2026-11-05, so the count stands at zero. In the 2026 sessions, ban bills passed one chamber in several states but none were enacted. Almost all 2027 sessions will happen before the July 1 deadline.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question names no single data series. The criteria point to news coverage of laws being signed. The closest trackers are the LifeMate list (Aug 2026) and the National Ag Law Center's state compilation.
- 2026-10-26: The latest tracker, a Tallow blog post citing LifeMate's August 2026 list, still shows exactly 8 ban states, all of them excluded: FL, AL, MS, MT, IN, NE, TX and SD. [tallow.app](https://tallow.app/blog/lab-grown-meat-bans-eight-states-which-expire-what-fda-cleared)
- 2026-08-15: LifeMate also lists 8 bans and names no pending bills. [lifematetech](https://lifematetech.com/articles/cultivated-meat-federal-clearance-state-bans)

## 2. Current status
- No new qualifying ban that I could find. Current value: 0.
- Louisiana SB 152 / HB 512 (2026): this is a trigger law that takes effect only if the US Supreme Court upholds such bans. No such ruling exists, so it does not count. [tallow.app](https://tallow.app/blog/lab-grown-meat-bans-eight-states-which-expire-what-fda-cleared)
- Laws that are labeling or partial measures do not count: Arizona HB 2762 (signed 2026-06-19), Ohio HB 10 (signed 2025-12-19, a school-purchase ban plus labeling) and Idaho SB 1270. [CSG Midwest](https://csgmidwest.org/2026/05/04/though-not-yet-on-grocery-shelves-lab-grown-meat-is-focus-of-new-laws-and-legislation/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-03/04: Midterms were described as a "huge sweep for Democrats." That could change who controls some governorships and legislatures in 2027. I did not check state-level results. [TSPR/NPR](https://www.tspr.org/npr-news/2026-11-04/where-voters-stand-on-state-ballot-measures-from-abortion-to-lgbtq-rights-to-guns)
- 2026-04-15: Kentucky HB 309, a full ban, passed a House committee in February. It was then recommitted to Appropriations & Revenue and saw no further action. [KY Legislature](https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/record/26RS/HB309.html); [LPM](https://www.lpm.org/news/2026-02-04/republicans-seek-to-ban-lab-grown-meat-before-it-hits-kentucky-shelves)
- 2026-03-30: South Dakota failed to override the veto of HB 1077, its stricter ban bill. [CSG Midwest](https://csgmidwest.org/2026/05/04/though-not-yet-on-grocery-shelves-lab-grown-meat-is-focus-of-new-laws-and-legislation/)
- 2026-03-27: Wisconsin Gov. Evers vetoed AB 554, a labeling and serving restriction rather than a full ban. [CSG Midwest](https://csgmidwest.org/2026/05/04/though-not-yet-on-grocery-shelves-lab-grown-meat-is-focus-of-new-laws-and-legislation/)
- 2026-03-12: South Dakota SB 124 was signed: a moratorium from 2026-07-01 to 2031-06-30. [SD Searchlight](https://southdakotasearchlight.com/2026/03/11/governor-signs-lab-grown-meat-moratorium-property-protections-crypto-national-security-bills/)
- 2026-02-24: South Carolina H.5096, a full ban, passed the House 110-0 and was referred to the Senate Agriculture committee, where it got no further action. The 2025-26 session has ended, so it presumably died. [SC Statehouse](https://www.scstatehouse.gov/billsearch.php?billnumbers=hb5096)
- 2026-02-23: Oklahoma SB 2121 passed Senate committee 9-3 on 2026-02-09 and was placed on General Order. I found no floor vote. A related bill, SB 96, is listed as "Engrossed - Dead" as of 2026-04-30. [Oklahoma Voice](https://oklahomavoice.com/2026/02/09/oklahoma-panel-passes-measure-to-ban-lab-grown-meat/); [LegiScan](https://legiscan.com/OK/text/SB96/2026)
- 2026-02-13: West Virginia HB 4462 passed the House 64-25. It then stalled in Senate Agriculture, and a tracker marks it dead. SB 225 never got past committee referrals. [WV Watch](https://westvirginiawatch.com/2026/02/10/effort-to-ban-lab-grown-meat-and-maybe-crab-rangoon-underway-in-wv-house/); [WV Legislature](https://bills.wvlegislature.gov/bill/history/2026/RS/SB225)
- 2026-01-27: Georgia SB 415 (Dickerson) was referred to committee with no further action found. Georgia HB 201 is marked dead. Georgia's 2025-26 term has ended. [GPB](https://www.gpb.org/news/2026/01/28/lawmakers-spotlight-georgia-senators-debate-lab-grown-meat-data-centers-and)
- Michigan HB 4083 and Illinois HB 15, both full bans, are stuck in committee. [CSG Midwest](https://csgmidwest.org/2026/05/04/though-not-yet-on-grocery-shelves-lab-grown-meat-is-focus-of-new-laws-and-legislation/)

## 4. Base rates
- 2024: 2 bans enacted (FL, AL).
- 2025: 5 bans enacted (MS, MT, IN, NE, TX).
- 2026: 1 ban enacted (SD), plus Louisiana's trigger law, which does not count.
- The trend has slowed since the 2025 peak. Many states that would most readily pass a ban already have one. Those still left have hit Senate bottlenecks (SC, WV, KY, OK) or opposing governors (WI).
- Most bans have been signed between March and June. That matches the window before July 1, 2027.
- In each 2026 session, 4 to 5 non-excluded states passed a ban through committee or one chamber, but none became law.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi, "Which states will ban lab-grown meat? (Before 2026)": Tennessee, Arizona and New Hampshire each at about 1%. This market has expired and its timeframe does not match. Kalshi's "Will Trump ban lab-grown meat?" is at 1%, which is not relevant to state laws.
- Manifold's "ban consumption of animal meat by 2050" market (31%) is unrelated.
- I found no market or expert forecast that matches this question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- January to June 2027: almost all state legislatures meet. New two-year sessions start in Georgia and South Carolina (bills would need to be refiled). Kentucky holds its short 30-day session. Oklahoma, West Virginia, Tennessee, Missouri, Wyoming, Arkansas and others also sit. I found no 2027 prefiled ban bills yet. Prefiling usually happens in November and December.
- Possible spillover from excluded states:
  - Indiana's moratorium ends on 2027-06-30.
  - Texas's ban ends on 2027-09-01, and its Fifth Circuit appeal is still pending.
  - Fights over renewing these could encourage similar bills elsewhere.
- The 2026-03 Eleventh Circuit ruling upholding Florida's ban gives sponsors legal cover. A Supreme Court ruling could trigger Louisiana's law, but none is expected before July 2027.
- Whether companies like Upside and Wildtype start selling to consumers could raise the issue's profile.
- The 2027 party makeup of governorships and legislatures is a factor after the 2026 midterms. I did not verify state-level results.

- 2026-08-15: LifeMate counts eight states that ban sales: FL, AL, MS, MT, IN, NE, TX and SD. All eight are excluded from this question. It lists Louisiana separately because its ban only takes effect on a trigger. [LifeMate](https://lifematetech.com/articles/cultivated-meat-federal-clearance-state-bans)

## 2. Current status

- Nothing has settled the question yet. I found no new, non-excluded state that has enacted a full sales ban that is actually in effect.
- 2026 (enacted): Louisiana's SB 152 bans the manufacture and sale of cell-cultured food, but it takes effect only after a final US Supreme Court ruling that such bans are constitutional. HB 512 has the same trigger. Under the fine print, neither counts unless that ruling happens. [NALC](https://nationalaglawcenter.org/food-law-in-the-states-2026-update-part-2/)
- 2026-03-23: The 11th Circuit upheld Florida's ban on preemption grounds. The appeal came from a denied preliminary injunction, so the case goes back to the district court. I found no evidence of a Supreme Court cert petition. This makes the Louisiana trigger unlikely to fire before July 2027, though I have not confirmed that on the dockets. [Florida Phoenix](https://floridaphoenix.com/2026/03/23/federal-appellate-panel-upholds-floridas-ban-on-lab-grown-meat/)
- Most state legislatures have adjourned for 2026. The bills that failed in 2026 will generally have to be reintroduced in 2027.

(b) **Status quo:** Zero. No new qualifying state ban has been enacted since the eight excluded states. Louisiana's trigger law does not count, and the Arizona, Ohio and Idaho measures are labeling or partial restrictions only.

(c) **Base rates:**
- 2024: 2 new states.
- 2025: 5 new states.
- 2026: 0 new non-excluded states. South Dakota's moratorium was its only enactment, and it is already excluded.

The trend has slowed sharply. The most eager states have already acted. In 2026, 4 to 5 remaining states advanced bills through committee or one chamber, but none got through both chambers and a governor. Seen across years, roughly half of recent sessions have produced at least one new state. The latest session produced none.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- South Carolina H.5096 passed the House 110-0 on 2026-02-24, then died in the Senate.
- West Virginia HB 4462 passed the House 64-25 in February 2026, then stalled in Senate Agriculture.
- Oklahoma SB 2121 cleared a Senate committee 9-3 on 2026-02-09 but never got a floor vote.
- Kentucky HB 309 was recommitted in spring 2026.
- Trackers as of Aug to Oct 2026 still list only 8 ban states.
- The March 2026 Eleventh Circuit ruling upholding Florida's ban gives sponsors legal cover.
- 2027 is the first year of new bienniums, so bills must be refiled.
- The 2026 midterms reportedly favored Democrats, which may slightly reduce the chances in swing states, though most candidate states remain solidly Republican.
- I found no matching prediction market.

(e) **Unexpected scenario:** Fights over renewing the expiring Indiana (June 2027) and Texas (September 2027) bans raise the issue's profile, or a company such as Upside or Wildtype launches retail sales. That could spark a coordinated 2027 push in which South Carolina, West Virginia, Oklahoma, Kentucky, Tennessee or Wyoming pass bans in quick succession, as happened in 2025, giving 2 to 4 new states.

**Reasoning:** I start from the status quo of 0, which is supported by the empty 2026 session. I then move upward because several states came within one chamber of passing, the 2027 sessions fall almost entirely within the window, and many Republican-trifecta states remain. Overall I put the chance of at least one new state at about 45%, with probability declining for each higher count.
